newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe opens Internet office to virtual visitors.
newsitem.headline: Juppe opens Internet office to virtual visitors.

text.p: Prime Minister Alain Juppe opened his office to virtual visitors on the Internet computer system on Thursday in a campaign to amplify France's voice in English-dominated cyberspace.

The web site, featuring a tricolour mouse as a guide, enables visitors to see computer-generated pictures of Juppe's Matignon offices and gardens in Paris and to read an official account of his achievements since he took office in May 1995.

"The government considers it very important for France to be present on these communications networks," Juppe told a group of about a dozen young computer enthusiasts as he inaugurated the site, "http://www.premier-ministre.gouv.fr."

The site includes portraits of all premiers since the Fifth Republic began in 1959 and five video clips from Juppe's private album, including a walk along a beach, talks with President Jacques Chirac and comments from his wife Isabelle.
The project, linked to a scheme to increase the use of French on the Internet, cost 600,000 francs ($120,000) and took five months to complete.
Visitors can use an electronic mail box to send suggestions to Juppe, a conservative whose popularity has slumped amid record unemployment in France.
